Struct SlabCache 

Source 
pub struct SlabCache {
    partial: Option<NonNull<SlabPageHeader>>,
    full: Option<NonNull<SlabPageHeader>>,
    empty: Option<NonNull<SlabPageHeader>>,
    layout: &'static SlabLayout,
}
Expand description

A size-class slab cache.

The cache owns a partial list, a full list, and one retained empty slab. All three hold slabs registered with SlabCache::add_slab. The bound layout is fixed at construction, so every slab in the cache has the same size, slot count, and slot size.

Fields§

§partial: Option<NonNull<SlabPageHeader>>

Slabs with at least one locally available slot.

§full: Option<NonNull<SlabPageHeader>>

Slabs with no locally available slot, though some may have pending remote frees.

§empty: Option<NonNull<SlabPageHeader>>

Retained empty slab, kept out of both lists.

§layout: &'static SlabLayout

Shared compile-time layout selected when the cache is constructed.

impl SlabCache

Slot allocation and slab memory management for SlabCache.

Source

pub const fn new(object_log2: usize, slab_log2: usize) -> AllocResult<Self>

Creates an empty size-class cache.

object_log2 and slab_log2 are the base-2 logarithms of the slot and slab sizes in bytes. They must select a power-of-two slot size from 8 to 2048 bytes and a power-of-two slab size from 4 to 256 KiB. Other values return AllocError::InvalidParam. The resulting cache holds no slab until the caller registers one with Self::add_slab.

Source

pub(crate) const fn with_layout(layout: &'static SlabLayout) -> Self

Binds an empty cache to one validated static slab layout record.

Used by crate::SlabAllocator, which selects the layout from its page-size policy.

Source

pub const fn layout(&self) -> &'static SlabLayout

Returns the immutable slab layout bound to this cache.

Source

pub unsafe fn add_slab(&mut self, base: VirtAddr, owner_cpu: u16) -> AllocResult

Registers slab memory with this cache.

Initializes the slab so that all of its slots are available, then adds it to the partial list. Returns AllocError::InvalidParam before memory access if the base is zero or is not aligned to SlabLayout::slab_size.

§Safety

An accepted base must identify exclusive writable slab memory of the bound slab size. Keep this memory valid until it is returned or all cache operations, slots, and remote producers end.

Source

pub fn alloc_object(&mut self) -> Option<VirtAddr>

Allocates one object slot.

Takes a slot from the first partial slab. If there is none, a full slab with pending remote frees is moved back to the partial list, and failing that the retained empty slab is reused. Returns None when the cache holds no slab that can supply a slot, which is the caller’s signal to register a new slab.

The caller serializes all operations through this cache.

Source

pub unsafe fn dealloc_object(&mut self, obj_addr: VirtAddr) -> Option<VirtAddr>

Releases an object slot to this cache.

Collects pending remote frees before judging whether the slab is empty, so that a slab emptied by remote frees is not mistaken for a partial one. Returns Some with the slab base when the slab became empty and the cache already retained another empty slab, leaving that slab for the caller to release. Its memory spans SlabLayout::slab_size bytes. Otherwise returns None, possibly after retaining this slab as the empty one.

§Safety

The address must identify one live slot belonging to this cache, released exactly once. The caller must serialize this call with all other operations through the cache.

Source

unsafe fn alloc_from_partial( &mut self, header: NonNull<SlabPageHeader>, ) -> VirtAddr

Allocates a slot from a partial slab.

Moves the slab to the full list if the final locally available slot is taken.

§Safety

The slab must belong to this cache’s partial list and have its bound slab layout. All owner accesses must be serialized and the slab memory must remain valid.

Source

unsafe fn push_front( head: &mut Option<NonNull<SlabPageHeader>>, slab: NonNull<SlabPageHeader>, )

Inserts a live unlinked slab at the front of an owner-managed list.

§Safety

All nodes must have live headers and valid links. The owner must have exclusive access to the links, and slab must not already belong to a list.

Source

unsafe fn remove( head: &mut Option<NonNull<SlabPageHeader>>, slab: NonNull<SlabPageHeader>, )

Removes one slab from an owner-managed doubly linked list.

§Safety

slab must belong to head, all links must identify live headers, and the owner must serialize all link updates.
